title: Apply a request key once
prompt: Complete IdempotentCounter. apply(key, delta) changes the total only the first time a nonempty key appears and returns true. Reusing a key returns false without changing total. Reject an empty key with std::invalid_argument. Inputs keep every total in int range. This is an in-memory, single-threaded model, not durable distributed storage.
signature: class IdempotentCounter: bool apply(const std::string& key, int delta); int total() const

tests.label: First request applies
tests.hint: Store both the key and the new total.

tests.label: Duplicate does not apply
tests.hint: The key determines duplication, even if its delta changes.

tests.label: Different keys
tests.hint: Distinct keys may both update the total.

tests.label: Empty key rejected
tests.hint: Reject an empty key before touching state.

hints: insert(...).second tells you whether the key was new.
Return false before adding the delta when the key already exists.
explanation: Remembering completed keys prevents repeated effects in this process. A production design also needs atomic persistence, retention rules, and concurrency control.
chapterTitle: Implementing Idempotency with a Durable Outbox and Inbox
